summary.headline: Raymond Realty Q1 FY27 booking value rose 129% YoY to INR700 crore; FY27 guidance of 20%+ presales growth and 17-19% EBITDA margin reiterated.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 booking value of INR700 crore (up 129% YoY), customer collections of INR550 crore (up 47%) and total income of INR536 crore (up 37%). EBITDA rose 70% YoY to INR70 crore, with margin expanding from 11% to 13%, which management attributed to upfront costs from four projects launched in Q4 FY26. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20%+ presales growth, 20%+ revenue growth, 17-19% EBITDA margin and 20%+ ROCE. JDAs now account for about 52% of INR52,000 crore total GDV, and a new Parel JDA with INR8,500 crore GDV was signed.

financial_highlights.change: Gross debt INR1,095 crore; cash INR271 crore
management said FY27 interest INR100-120 crore

segments.name: JDA (asset-light) portfolio
segments.commentary: Eight JDA projects with combined GDV of INR27,000 crore (52% of total GDV); 64% of Q1 presales came from JDAs. Four launched projects (Bandra East, BKC, Wadala, Sion) carry INR11,500 crore revenue potential, INR2,900 crore cumulative sales and about INR692 crore collections.

segments.name: Owned land (Thane, 100 acres)
segments.commentary: 65 acres under active development with 6.7 million sq ft RERA carpet area and INR16,500 crore revenue potential; INR9,400 crore sold and INR7,460 crore collected to date. Contributed 36% of Q1 booking value; 11 towers (about 4,000 homes) delivered. Management expects own-land margins of 25-26%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the top execution priorities and biggest risks (demand, regulation, competition)?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is execution of Q4 FY26 launches; demand 'pleasantly' above expectations; cost pressures from global wars seen as temporary, with contingencies budgeted over 5-6 year project cycles; policy stable with DCR 2034 and supportive Maharashtra government.

qa_highlights.question: How is capital allocation and funding aligned with the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt-to-equity 0.7x versus internal 1x ceiling; AIFs offering SPV-level capital as an option; equity seen as last resort; cost of debt has only declined.

qa_highlights.question: Parel project ticket size, saleable area, launch timing and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Launch about 18 months away; ticket sizes INR6-20 crore; total GDV INR8,500 crore; realisation not disclosed beyond GDV.

qa_highlights.question: Mahim launch timing and GDV, and H2 launch calendar?
qa_highlights.answer: Two Mahim projects: first ~Nov-Dec 2026 (~INR2,500 crore GDV), second Feb-Mar 2027 (~INR2,100-2,200 crore); six of eight JDAs to be launched by FY27 end.

qa_highlights.question: Purpose of TenX Mahalakshmi Limited incorporation?
qa_highlights.answer: Incorporated as an SPV in anticipation of new projects; no deal signed yet, to be disclosed when signed.

qa_highlights.question: JDA vs owned-land economics, margins and ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: JDA capital need INR300-350 crore per project, peak INR450-500 crore for Parel; own land margin 25-26%, JDA ~20% scaling up in FY28; ROCE guided at 20%+.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost trajectory and debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt INR824 crore, gross debt INR1,095 crore, cash INR271 crore; FY27 interest INR100-120 crore; Q1 ~INR47 crore; government dues interest at 8-9% explained as part of finance cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why no PAT guidance and what about cash profit and operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: No net profit or operating cash flow guidance given; management will revert on PAT growth impact of higher interest.

qa_highlights.question: Demand softness and Home Fest purpose?
qa_highlights.answer: No softness seen; Home Fest is an annual monsoon event for top-of-funnel; response described as good.

qa_highlights.question: Expansion beyond MMR and JDA control terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus remains MMR and Maharashtra; Pune studied but returns did not meet criteria. Company insists on 100% development control in JDAs with step-in rights.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales growth of 20%+ YoY reiterated as a minimum commitment.
FY27 revenue (total turnover) growth of minimum 20% YoY.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 17-19%; management said it will land somewhere in between, aiming close to 20% over time.
FY27 ROCE of 20% or higher; management said FY22-FY26 ROCE was above 25%.
Interest cost for FY27 guided at INR100-120 crore (management said it expects it below Q1's ~INR47 crore in later quarters); exact figure to be disclosed later.
Margins expected to normalise over Q2-Q4 as Q4 FY26 launches cross revenue recognition thresholds; JDAs expected at ~20% margin and own land at 25-26%, with JDA margins scaling up in FY28.
Two Mahim JDA projects to launch: first around Nov-Dec 2026 (GDV ~INR2,500 crore), second Feb-Mar 2027 (GDV ~INR2,100-2,200 crore); six of eight JDAs expected launched by end FY27.
capex_capacity: Total GDV INR52,000 crore: owned Thane land INR25,000 crore and JDAs INR27,000 crore (eight projects, ~52% of GDV).

Thane 100-acre parcel: 65 acres under active development, ~6.7 million sq ft RERA carpet area, INR16,500 crore revenue potential; INR9,400 crore sold, INR7,460 crore collected; 11 towers (~4,000 homes) delivered.

Four launched JDAs (Bandra East, BKC, Wadala, Sion): ~2.8 million sq ft RERA carpet, INR11,500 crore revenue potential, INR2,900 crore cumulative sales, ~INR692 crore collections; mostly at excavation stage.
Parel JDA: GDV INR8,500 crore, ~1.7 million sq ft carpet area, launch in about 18 months; ticket sizes INR6-20 crore; mix of Address by GS and Invictus by GS.
JDA capital requirement ~INR300-350 crore per project of INR2,000 crore+ GDV, rising to INR450-500 crore peak for Parel; deposit of 10-15% of land value at signing.
Unsold launched inventory ~INR15,700 crore; unlaunched GDV ~INR24,000 crore.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 booking value INR700 crore, +129% YoY from INR306 crore; management said Q1 came in slightly above internal expectations.
Q1 presales: 64% from asset-light JDA projects; roughly two-thirds from MMR and one-third from Thane.
Thane land contributed 36% of Q1 booking value.
Brands: TenX, Address by GS, Invictus by GS; management cited strong brand pull in Thane and wider MMR.
Home Fest (monsoon event, run for three years) said to generate footfall; management said ~20% converts during event and ~80% over the following two months.
Management said no softness seen in any project; cost pressure from global conditions noted as temporary.
risks_watch: Cost inflation from global conditions over 5-6 year project lives; management says buffers are budgeted but no quantification given.
Interest burden rising with debt drawn (gross debt INR1,095 crore vs INR380 crore a year earlier per analyst); PAT growth not guided.
Early-stage JDA margins (~20% target) and Q1 margin dip from Q4 FY26 launch costs; full-year margin depends on Q2-Q4 normalisation.
Parel (INR8,500 crore GDV) and Mahim launches depend on approvals; Parel is ~18 months from launch and two recent JDAs have not started approvals.
Thane share of bookings expected to fall as MMR launches scale, though absolute Thane sales may stay flat.
Institutional holding decline flagged by an individual investor; management cites market-cap and mandate constraints and new IR hire.
Borrowing/interest disclosures pending: FY27 interest figure and government dues interest breakdown to be published.
key_quotes: So, we are firmly and completely on track to achieving our full year EBITDA margin guidance of 17% to 19%.

So, the current year's initial profitability will reflect the upfront marketing and construction setup costs, and the margins will progressively normalize over subsequent quarters as project construction crosses revenue recognition thresholds
The net debt at the end of Q1 closed at INR824 crores, maintaining a healthy debt-to-equity ratio of 0.7x in Q1 FY27.
Typically, the kind of deals that we are signing today, INR 2,000 crores upward, the ballpark number for each JDA, the capital required is somewhere in the range of INR 300 crores to INR350 crores.
summary.management_tone: "Confident and upbeat on demand, guidance and debt discipline, with a few hedged answers. Management was evasive on PAT growth, the exact FY27 interest number and the 'Kunjal' borrowings question, promising to revert later."

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of minimum 20% and presales growth of 20%+, backed by 52,000 crore GDV pipeline (Thane owned land plus eight JDAs), 8,500 crore Parel JDA and Mahim JDA launches due Nov 2026 to Mar 2027, with Q1 revenue up 37% and bookings up 129%, though no explicit capacity or sales-timing schedule beyond project launches was given.
